article.title: From Prediction to Action: Why Business Value Needs More Than Accuracy

paragraphs.en: Predictive accuracy is only one step between a model and business value. A model may rank customers correctly yet create little value if the organization cannot act on its predictions or if the chosen action is expensive. Consider a retention model that identifies customers likely to churn. High churn probability does not mean a retention offer will change their behavior. Some customers may leave regardless of contact, while others would stay without an incentive. The decision problem requires expected incremental benefit, intervention cost, capacity, and possible side effects. Thresholds should therefore be linked to economics. If a call costs money and the call center has limited capacity, the organization should prioritize cases where expected value is highest, not simply everyone above an arbitrary probability. Outcome models and treatment-effect models answer different questions. The former predict what is likely to happen; the latter attempt to estimate what changes because of an action. Even without advanced causal modeling, teams can improve decision quality by running randomized tests around model-driven policies. Compare a model-based strategy with an appropriate alternative and measure incremental outcomes, not only response among selected customers. Calibration matters when probabilities enter expected-value calculations, while ranking matters when only a fixed number of cases can be handled. Operational constraints, customer experience, fairness, and regulatory rules can also change the optimal policy. A technically strong model can therefore be the wrong business system if the surrounding decision rule is poorly designed. Teams should document the prediction target, available actions, costs, benefits, constraints, and evaluation metric before deployment. They should monitor both model performance and realized business outcomes after launch. The most useful question is not “How accurate is the model?” but “Does using this model lead to better decisions than the alternative?” That shift connects data science to the counterfactual logic of decision making and prevents teams from treating an offline score as the final objective. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本篇從樣本、selection、分群、時間資訊與decision value 說明，為什麼分析不能只看表面指標。重點是先確認資料如何產生、哪些人被納入、資訊在何時可取得，以及觀察到的關係是否真的能支持商業結論。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：sample、selection、segment、情報の時点、decision valueの観点から、表面的なmetricだけでは分析できない理由を説明する。data generating process、対象population、情報取得時点、観察関係がbusiness conclusionを支持する範囲を確認することが重要である。
